notes.author: H. Okonkwo
notes.text: Provider credits are pre-purchased each quarter and expire unused, so MOD-01 runs ahead of actual consumption early in a quarter.

risks.title: Provider token spend outruns pre-purchased credits
risks.description: Consumption growth is driven by internal teams with uncapped keys - spend can outrun the credit envelope inside a single quarter.
risks.mitigation: Per-key budget caps and hard spend stops shipped in July; weekly burn review with finance.

risks.title: Upstream rate limits apply per organisation, not per key
risks.description: One team's batch job can exhaust the shared quota and throttle every other caller through the gateway.
risks.mitigation: Automatic failover across three providers plus request shaping at the edge; per-organisation quota dashboards.

risks.title: Prompt logging retains request bodies beyond data residency commitments
risks.description: Full request and response bodies were retained for 30 days in a single region, which exceeds what customer contracts allow.
risks.mitigation: Retention cut to 72 hours with field-level redaction; data protection impact assessment updated.

risks.title: Single-region control plane is a single point of failure
risks.description: Routing, keys and quota state all live in one region - a regional outage takes every tenant offline.
risks.mitigation: Second region live since September with a tested 11-minute failover.

risks.title: Streaming responses truncate under the new load balancer
risks.description: Long completions were cut short for six days before detection because buffering defaults changed.
risks.mitigation: Buffering defect fixed and covered by a streaming conformance test in CI.

risks.title: Provider commercial terms worsen at renewal
risks.description: Two of the three upstream contracts renew in Q1 2027 with volume commitments set before demand grew.
risks.mitigation: Renewal negotiations opened early with committed-volume pricing benchmarked across three providers.

risks.title: Customer API keys are stored without automatic rotation
risks.description: Keys are hashed at rest but there is no rotation endpoint, so a leaked key stays valid until someone notices.
risks.mitigation: Rotation endpoint scoped for Q4; per-key scopes and last-used telemetry already shipped.

risks.title: Upstream model deprecations break pinned model IDs
risks.description: Customers pin exact model identifiers; a provider retiring two of them in November would break those integrations.
risks.mitigation: Alias layer maps pinned IDs onto current models; deprecation calendar tracked per provider.

risks.title: Usage metering lags real spend, so chargeback is disputed
risks.description: Metering trailed provider invoices by up to 36 hours, so per-team cost attribution could not be reconciled.
risks.mitigation: Metering pipeline moved to 15-minute batches and reconciled against provider invoices monthly.

risks.title: SOC 2 Type II evidence collection behind schedule
risks.description: Evidence for five of nineteen controls is still collected by hand during the observation window.
risks.mitigation: Evidence automation in place for fourteen controls; weekly review with the auditor until the window closes.

risks.title: Latency-aware routing degrades quality on long-context requests
risks.description: Routing on latency alone sends long-context requests to whichever model answers fastest, not the one that answers best.

risks.title: Contract engineering ramp-down leaves single-owner areas
risks.description: Billing and two provider adapters have one owner each once Northcape rolls off in October.
risks.mitigation: Knowledge transfer plan with paired ownership for the billing and adapter layers.

reports.author: Arjun Mehta
reports.executive_summary: Conduit reached internal general availability in February and is now the default path to model providers for five pilot teams. The unified chat completion API is live in front of two upstream providers, availability was 99.94% across March, and the platform served an average of 41 million tokens a day in the final month of the quarter. Spend tracks a little under profile because the security audit started later than planned. The watch items are cost visibility and shared rate limits: metering still lags real spend, and upstream quotas turn out to apply to the whole organisation rather than to individual keys.
progress: Unified /v1/chat completion API released, with adapters for Northstar and Corvus behind a single request format.
Internal general availability reached on 27 February with five pilot teams migrated off direct provider SDKs.
Availability of 99.94% in March against a 99.9% internal objective; p95 latency 820ms end to end.
Usage metering pipeline delivering per-key token counts, currently with a lag of up to 36 hours.

reports.author: Arjun Mehta
reports.executive_summary: Conduit moves to amber. Token consumption grew far faster than the plan assumed once the gateway opened past the pilot teams: an unbudgeted evaluation harness run by the search team, together with internal keys that still carry no spend cap, pushed pass-through provider cost materially ahead of profile. A rate-limit cascade on 14 May took availability for the month to 99.71%, and a buffering regression truncated long streaming responses for six days before anyone noticed. Delivery itself is healthy - a third provider is live behind automatic failover and SOC 2 Type I was awarded in June. No financial position is included this quarter: a full reforecast is in progress with finance and will accompany the Q3 report.
progress: Helion adapter shipped, putting three providers behind automatic failover with health-based ejection.
Per-key budget caps designed and approved at review; build moved into Q3.
SOC 2 Type I report awarded on 12 June; the Type II observation window opened on 1 June.
Streaming moved onto the new load balancer, where a buffering regression truncated long completions for six days before detection.

milestones.comment: Design approved; build moved to Q3.

The 14 May cascade is not fully explained: the runbook assumed per-key rate limits, but the provider applies them per organisation.
Prompt logging retains full request bodies for 30 days, which has not been reviewed against our data residency commitments.
next_period: Ship per-key budget caps and hard spend stops.
Complete the cost reforecast and take it to the steering group.
Decide whether to fund the multi-region control plane from contingency.

reports.author: Arjun Mehta
reports.executive_summary: Conduit stays amber but is trending back to green. Budget caps and hard spend stops shipped on 22 July and slowed month-on-month provider spend growth from 61% to 9%, with runaway consumption incidents down from seven in the previous quarter to one. Latency-aware routing cut p95 from 1,140ms to 690ms, and the control plane now runs in two regions with a failover exercise completed in eleven minutes. The provider token line has nonetheless passed its own budget, at just under 1.6 million against a 1.45 million line, and a virement from contingency is requested. The programme as a whole remains under budget. Attention now moves to the November model deprecations and to closing SOC 2 Type II.
progress: Per-key budget caps and hard spend stops shipped on 22 July; runaway consumption incidents fell from seven in Q2 to one in Q3.
Latency-aware routing cut p95 latency from 1,140ms to 690ms while holding availability at 99.89%.
Multi-region control plane live from 4 September, with a failover exercise completed in eleven minutes.
Prompt log retention cut from 30 days to 72 hours with field-level redaction, closing the data residency gap.
